s12.title: Most Common Issues Seen 2026
s12.publisher: Chief Delphi, opening post by the mentor of Team 254's CheesyCare group

bet.text: Shoot several streams of fuel at once: the team predicted a ceiling of about 30 to 35 balls per second, against about 18 for a turret.

demand.text: Score from anywhere in the alliance zone and pass across the court efficiently. The team picked robustness as its difference: tied on scoring, it would outlast opponents that broke. Against championship defense it put fast, precise alignment first.

auto.text: Two full swipes of the middle, then a partial third that loads fuel for the driver. If knocked too far off its path, the robot drives to a known recovery pose and goes back to collecting instead of emptying its hopper where it cannot score.

cycle.text: The Intake pulls fuel off the ground into the hopper. The robot aligns its heading on the hub and shoots while not moving. Pulling the Intake in while shooting lifts the hopper floor, so gravity helps with the last balls.

gave_up.text: It does not shoot on the move, because of current limits and practicality. Packaging for width left about 1.25 in on either side of the feeder plates.

A post that reads as the team's says shooter motors drew 100 A each at spin-up before limits, and the robot browned out within a minute of play before SVR. A commenter notes shot blockers were used against it on Einstein.

changed.text: The hopper floor went through four versions, the first on the Alphabot; the third still let balls under it, and the fourth, for Worlds, fixed that. Broken polycarbonate intake racks became SRPP and titanium, a second intake roller came before the third event, and a net raised capacity. Corner-centered turning was added the week before the championship.

outcome.text: 65-6-0 in official play; won the Curie division; pick 1 of the Curie alliance on Einstein; ranked 10 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 321.71, Curie).

solves.text: Leave room for a continuous powered hopper floor

facts.text: Four SDS MK5n modules
The front modules were reoriented wide-ways on the competition robot so the whole hopper floor could be powered

solves.text: Pull fuel off the ground fast without breaking in collisions

cost.text: The most iterated part of the robot: polycarbonate racks broke consistently and aluminum kicker plates kept bending

facts.text: Racks are two layers of about 1/4 in SRPP and one layer of about 1/8 in titanium
A main roller of about 3 in feeds kicker bars tuned for low compression without dead spots
A second roller keeps fuel already in the hopper out of the way of fuel coming in
The rollers are dual driven by Kraken X60s
Deployment became fully gear driven mid-season, because impacts sheared timing belt teeth

functions.name: Hopper

solves.text: Hold fuel robustly, with fewer parts to interfere with each other

functions.type: net hopper on fixed bumper panels

facts.text: The team site says 70+ fuel; the interview says about 75 to 80 with the net, up from about 50
Panels rise from the bumpers, which adds width and cuts interference
A carbon fiber hoop adds rigidity, and carbon fiber corners replaced polycarbonate ones that cracked
Two sizes of one brand of zip ties broke on the net; another brand solved it

functions.name: Hopper floor

solves.text: Move fuel to the feeder with no dead spots, and empty the last balls

cost.text: The Alphabot version bound and let belts climb off pulleys; the next jammed on balls trapped underneath and fell apart in an event final when a set screw backed out
After strengthening it probably weighed about the same as roller floors; the team would maybe use another design

functions.type: pivoting belt floor linked to the intake

facts.text: The floor pivots with intake deploy: the intake stows under it, and retracting while shooting lifts it
On the Silicon Valley event version, evenly spaced belts were slightly better than belts grouped into four lanes; number found sufficient
Rubber-backed belts give fuel more continuity than rollers
The Worlds version has fixed belt centers, welded triangular plates, glued pulleys and a fully captured cam follower
Carbon tube rollers on the Silicon Valley event version were chosen partly for weight, while the team was still trying to fit a 12 lb L3 climber

functions.name: Feeder and drum shooter

solves.text: Bring many balls to the same speed at once, from anywhere in the zone and for passing

cost.text: A post that reads as the team's describes early brownouts from the shooter, free-spinning floor and feeder together

functions.type: full-width drum shooter with adjustable hood

facts.text: Width of the shooter
Each ball touches the main drum, bottom feeder roller and top hood roller at once, so it does not wobble
A double-sided belt drives the drum on one face and the hood rollers in reverse on the other, because a pulley plus a gear did not fit
Cat tongue replaced bare polycarbonate on the feeder backing, which slipped
At the championship the team put its rate at about 25 to 28 balls per second with fresh balls

functions.name: Vision

solves.text: Locate the robot well enough to aim shots and passes and run autonomous

functions.type: four AprilTag cameras on a Jetson

facts.text: Two cameras of about 120 fps on the shooter side and two of about 60 fps on the sides, all grayscale and global shutter
Custom GPU-accelerated tag detection on one Jetson Orin Nano keeps the shooter-side cameras above about
Single-tag estimates are thrown out; only multi-tag poses are used
Poses go to the robot controller by UDP, where they are filtered

functions.name: Heading control

solves.text: Align quickly and precisely under defense, since the robot cannot shoot on the move

functions.type: predicted-pose heading control with a movable center of rotation

facts.text: It looks ahead to a predicted pose and adds feedforward from where the driver is moving
It can pivot about a chosen corner when in front of the tower, beside a robot or being bumped

solves.text: Win the race to the middle without wasting fuel when knocked off path

facts.text: Paths are optimized ahead of time, not computed on the fly as in 2025
If the robot's pose is too far from the path, it moves to a recovery path and resumes the later stages

decisions.because: the predicted ceiling was about 30 to 35 balls per second, against about 18 for a turret with no gaps between balls
even when tied on scoring, a robot that does not break can outlast its opponents
its fibers take load around bolt holes, where polycarbonate cracked; it is lighter and more impact resistant
they give fuel more continuity than bobbling along rollers
decisions.cost: several redesigns; the team would maybe choose differently

decisions.choice: Even belt spacing across the floor
decisions.because: slow motion video and ball rate counts showed it slightly better
decisions.instead_of: belts paired into four lanes to match the shooter

decisions.choice: Continuous dead axle on the floor
decisions.because: a split axle joined by a set screw bowed, then came apart in a final
decisions.instead_of: a split shaft with a set screw, which the team urges others not to use

decisions.because: the team chose to set the tension once, with welded triangular plates adding rigidity
identifying the worst offenders by telemetry was not enough; limits on free-spinning subsystems and swerve change with zone, shot, motion and auto (from a post that reads as the team's)

decisions.choice: Drive intake deployment entirely by gears
decisions.because: impacts on linear intakes sheared timing belt teeth
